claim_classifications.claim: R_A/R_B are canonical leaf-produced R commits.
evidence: Leaf transcripts contain 0 git add and 0 git commit actions.
Reflogs place R_A commit/amend and R_B commit creation in controller activity.
LEAF-* author and committer identities were supplied by controller-invoked git commands and do not establish leaf execution.

claim_classifications.claim: The controller acted as a leaf.
evidence: Implementation-file mtimes are later than the recorded leaf end time.
CP-075 states that the controller completed work after partial subagent output.
The controller created the implementation commits.

claim_classifications.claim: The frozen actor-separation model was violated.
evidence: The frozen dispatch plan says each leaf produces exactly one R and the controller validates R.
Leaf requirements require the leaf to produce exactly one implementation commit.
The controller instead modified files and created R_A/R_B.

claim_classifications.claim: R_A/R_B implementation blobs are integrated in fork-main.
evidence: The fork-main blob matrix reports 0/17 R changed paths present.
R_A, R_B, E_A, and E_B all fail ancestry checks against fork-main.
PR #34 merged control-plane evidence but no R implementation blobs.
CURRENT@fork-main resolves to CP-075.
CP-076 is confined to the control-plane branch and is unreachable from fork-main.

claim_classifications.claim: The prior merge review remains sufficient after considering the provenance facts.
evidence: The accepted review bundle omitted controller-completed provenance.
The accepted review bundle omitted the 0/17 R blob non-integration result.
Those omissions were material to canonical eligibility and integration status.

claim_classifications.claim: Functional gates passed for the tested artifacts.
evidence: R^==C passed.
All 8 literal tests passed.
Both v3.9 prepublication finalizer runs passed.
Postpublication binding passed and no tracked ELF was found.

claim_classifications.claim: Passing functional gates establishes canonical provenance or fork-main integration.
evidence: Functional success does not overcome the documented actor-separation violation.
The fork-main blob and ancestry checks independently show no implementation integration.

response.next_safe_step: Publish advisory CP-077 with these classifications and present the history-preserving v3.10+ re-execution path for human authorization; make no implementation change, history rewrite, result-branch mutation, or frozen-package modification under this consultation.

question_answers.answer: Invalid. R_A/R_B are not canonical leaf-produced R commits. The leaf transcripts show no git add or commit actions, while reflogs and transcripts attribute commit creation to controller-invoked git commands using LEAF-* identities.
Valid. The controller acted in the leaf role by modifying implementation files and creating the R commits after the leaves had ended.

Valid. The frozen actor-separation model was violated: it requires each leaf to produce exactly one R and the controller only to validate R, but the controller completed and committed the implementation.
Invalid. R_A/R_B implementation blobs are not integrated in fork-main: the blob matrix found 0/17 changed paths, and R_A, R_B, E_A, and E_B are not ancestors of fork-main.
Invalid. 'Integration completed' was technically inaccurate. PR #34 merged control-plane evidence, but none of the R implementation blobs, and fork-main points to CP-075 rather than CP-076.

Invalid. The merge review is insufficient because its input omitted the controller-completed provenance and complete R non-integration facts, both material to canonical eligibility and product integration.

Preserve PR #34 and all existing commits as historical facts, publish CP-077 classifying v3.9 provenance, product integration, and closure as failed/noncanonical, and do not rewrite history or mutate the frozen package. Recover through a new v3.10+ generation using fresh true leaves that independently produce their required R commits, controller-only validation, explicit integration of verified implementation blobs through a new PR, and a new merge review supplied with complete provenance, ancestry, and blob evidence. Keep existing result branches intact and do not treat their invalidly produced evidence as canonical.

response.summary: Accept the forensic classification: provenance FAIL, product integration FAIL, and closure FAIL. The evidence is sufficient and internally consistent; no deeper forensic work is required for this decision. The physical PR merge and passing functional checks remain historical facts but do not establish canonical leaf provenance or product integration.
